Generality lens: the move is stated beyond the 2^n mod 7 example. applicability.goal_shape abstracts to 'a congruence a ≡ b [MOD m] (or equality) where a can be rewritten so that a periodic subterm appears, collapsing to a residue depending on n only through n % k'; use_when/avoid_when are general, not number-theory-specific. Known-use claim 4 (verified) shows the calc-chain works over two further relation kinds (↔ in q1a L42-47, ≡ in q1b L53-55). When-not-to-use lists three specific, honest conditions (non-rewrite link that won't sit on one calc line; period not decide-closable i.e. symbolic base/modulus; congruence not respecting the operation used). Consequences are honest and specific: four link sub-goals, no named lemma, calc elaborator supplies transitivity, the one substantive obligation is the decide-discharged period, and the =/≡ mix typechecks only via reflexive implication so reordering breaks. No grounds to object under this lens.
